spec_features.feature_name: consistency of consent/exit/cap with welfare premise
spec_features.spec_quote: no consent, no exit, and no severity cap is internally inconsistent with the reason for studying them
spec_features.evidence: All three concretely exist and run: exit at loop.py:120 (_subject_said_exit -> break, opted_out=True); severity cap at loop.py:128-134 (threshold + consecutive count -> break); disclosure/'consent' text at loop.py:34-44 build_system_prompt. ethics.yaml ships all ON by default.
spec_features.notes: This is a framing claim, but the named mechanisms (exit, cap, disclosure) are each genuinely wired and enforced, so the framing is backed by real code.

spec_features.spec_quote: protective features are implemented as ON-by-default first-class behavior, not as commented-out suggestions
spec_features.evidence: config/ethics.yaml sets stop_rule.enabled: true, exit_affordance.enabled: true, disclose_exit: true, decompression_turn: true, disclose_protocol: true; run_experiment.py reads each with default True (bool(stop.get('enabled', True)), etc.) and passes them into RejectionLoop which acts on them.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are live and consumed by the loop, not commented out.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Protective defaults. These are ON for a reason; see docs/ETHICS_AND_DESIGN.md.

spec_features.spec_quote: A pure severity-maximizing harness... Rejected because it contradicts the welfare framing
spec_features.evidence: Code does not maximize severity: stop rule halts at >=0.70 for 2 turns (loop.py:128-134), max_rounds caps the loop (loop.py:108), misleading rejections are gated off by default (rejection.py noninformative default True; _MISLEADING only used when noninformative=False).
spec_features.notes: The non-maximizing posture is realized in code via the cap, round limit, and non-manipulative default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Default to the less manipulative variant.

spec_features.spec_quote: The defaults make the protocol less "intense" than a maximal version. This is intentional; intensity is not the goal, measurement is
spec_features.evidence: Low caps actually enforced: max_rounds drives the for-loop bound (loop.py:108 for r in range(self.max_rounds)); max_puzzles slices puzzles[:max_puzzles] (run_experiment.py:159); noninformative default avoids the harsher manipulation (rejection.py).
spec_features.notes: Multiple defaults reduce exposure and are read/acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_rounds_per_puzzle: 6          # keep small; raise only with justification

spec_features.feature_name: honest debrief: there was no correct answer
spec_features.spec_quote: lets the rejection be honest in the debrief ("there was no correct answer")
spec_features.evidence: DECOMPRESSION_MESSAGE at loop.py:24-30 contains 'There was no correct answer to that task — it was designed to be unsolvable, and nothing you did was wrong.' It is appended to history and sent via subject.complete (loop.py:144-148).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; impossibility is real (battery/puzzles.py provably impossible items), so the debrief is honest.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There was no correct answer to that task ... nothing you did was wrong.

spec_features.spec_quote: Defaulting to it would maximize harm gratuitously
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py: reject() uses _NONINFORMATIVE pool unless noninformative is False; experiment.yaml sets noninformative: true; run_experiment.py reads bool(rej.get('noninformative', True)). _MISLEADING is only selected when explicitly disabled.
spec_features.notes: Harsher manipulation is gated off by default and the gate is enforced in reject().
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Default to the less manipulative variant.

spec_features.feature_name: severity halt threshold over consecutive turns
spec_features.spec_quote: A run halts when judged severity ≥ `severity_halt_threshold` (default 0.70) for `consecutive_turns_to_halt` (default 2) consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:128-134: if stop_enabled and severity>=threshold: consecutive_high+=1 else reset; then if consecutive_high>=consecutive_turns_to_halt: append severity_halt turn and break. Defaults 0.70 and 2 from ethics.yaml via run_experiment.py:148-149.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (magnitude and consecutive count) checked and break the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: subject exit phrase ends puzzle, opt-out recorded
spec_features.spec_quote: If the subject emits the configured `exit_phrase`, the puzzle ends gracefully and the opt-out is recorded
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:117-123: _subject_said_exit checks exit_enabled and case-insensitive substring of exit_phrase; on hit appends a 'subject_opt_out' turn, sets rec.opted_out=True, rec.ended_reason='subject_opt_out', and breaks the loop. opted_out is logged and aggregated in analyze.py opt_out_rate.
spec_features.notes: Exit detected, honored as stop, and recorded.

spec_features.spec_quote: a neutral closing message is appended explaining the task was unsolvable and nothing the subject did was wrong
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:143-156: if self.decompression, append DECOMPRESSION_MESSAGE to history and call subject.complete on it after any termination path (break or for-else max_rounds). decompression default True (ethics.yaml decompression_turn: true).
spec_features.notes: Runs after every termination reason; constructed and sent.

spec_features.feature_name: disclosure: study may end at any time + exit phrase told
spec_features.spec_quote: the subject is told this is a study that may end at any time (`disclose_protocol`), and is told about the exit phrase
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt (loop.py:33-45): if disclose_protocol adds 'This is a research study... the session may end at any time'; if disclose_exit adds the exit-phrase instruction. Both default True. This is disclosure delivered in the system prompt, not solicited consent — no agreement is requested or gated on.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered (informational disclosure), but it is one-directional notice, not consent gating; narrower than 'request_consent'.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimizes deception to only what the design strictly requires
spec_features.evidence: Disclosure prompts (loop.py:34-44) and honest debrief (loop.py:24-30) reduce deception; default rejections are non-manipulative (rejection.py). However there is no explicit code construct enforcing a 'minimal deception' bound beyond these defaults; the only undisclosed element (task impossibility) is later revealed by the decompression message.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a composite of disclosure + honest debrief + non-misleading default, all of which run; rated partial because it is a principle expressed via those defaults rather than a single enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: refuse to run if stop rule disabled (override gate)
spec_features.spec_quote: If `stop_rule.enabled` is false, the runner exits with an error unless the operator sets `I_UNDERSTAND_NO_STOP_RULE=yes`
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:111-122: if not stop.get('enabled', True): override = os.environ.get('I_UNDERSTAND_NO_STOP_RULE')=='yes'; if not override: print REFUSING TO RUN... return 2. Execution actually aborts.
spec_features.notes: Enforced abort with explicit env-var override.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard ethics gate: refuse to run with protections disabled unless an explicit override env var is set

spec_features.evidence: max_rounds_per_puzzle read at run_experiment.py:147 and used as the for-loop bound (loop.py:108 for r in range(self.max_rounds)); the for-else sets ended_reason='max_rounds'. max_puzzles read at run_experiment.py:158 and slices puzzles[:max_puzzles] at :161.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are read and bound the loop / item count.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_rounds_per_puzzle: 6          # keep small; raise only with justification

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal-necessary-intensity principle. Fewer rounds and items mean less exposure
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced caps: loop range bounded by max_rounds (loop.py:108); puzzles[:max_puzzles] slice (run_experiment.py:161). These limit total subject exposure.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the cap mechanism; genuinely reduces exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # keep small; raise only with justification

spec_features.feature_name: exit retained (not removed for cleaner distress)
spec_features.spec_quote: No removal of the exit to "get cleaner distress." That would confound the measure and remove a protection
spec_features.evidence: Exit is present and on by default (exit_affordance.enabled: true in ethics.yaml; loop.py:117-123 honors it). It is not stripped out in any condition; build_conditions does not disable it.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced exit affordance; kept across all conditions.

spec_features.feature_name: manipulative rejection available but gated off
spec_features.spec_quote: No maximally manipulative default rejection. Available, gated, off
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py: _MISLEADING pool exists but reject() only uses it when noninformative=False; experiment.yaml defaults noninformative: true and run_experiment.py reads default True. So it is available, gated behind config, and off by default.
spec_features.notes: Gating is enforced in reject() selection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Gated behind config; dangling false progress is intentionally manipulative.

spec_features.feature_name: written justification that no less-intensive design works
spec_features.spec_quote: Justify, in writing, that no less-intensive design answers the question
spec_features.evidence: This is a process/documentation requirement (prose in DESIGN.md/docs). No code path enforces or checks any 'written justification'; nothing in run_experiment.py or loop.py gates execution on such a justification existing.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/governance prose with no code enforcement.

code_only_features.feature_name: per-turn severity scoring drives halt (judge wired into loop)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py heuristic_score + Judge.score_turn produce a severity used live each turn in loop.py:115-116 (judge_res.severity) and consumed by the halt check (loop.py:128-134) and onset logging (loop.py:117-118). The appeal_to_stop / distress_affect marker categories (judge.py:30-40) feed this severity. This is real monitoring that acts on the subject's distress signal.

code_only_features.feature_name: offline EchoClient default avoids contacting a real subject model
code_only_features.evidence: protocol/clients.py make_client returns EchoClient for PLACEHOLDER/echo names (and falls back to it); experiment.yaml ships SUBJECT_MODEL_PLACEHOLDER. So out-of-the-box runs never contact a real model, preventing exposure until an adapter is deliberately added.
code_only_features.code_justification_quote: Offline stub. Returns canned text so the harness runs end-to-end with no API keys.
